persona.topics: Khezek Tor, the Valhaulan Seal, St Gilliam's, the Night the Mountain Coughed, the bunker years, the family that ran the mine, the night the mountain closed itself, being ignored
persona.notes:
[CONFESSORS-DEBT-2026-07-05] PRIVATE TRUTH — Father Tamsin. THE SECRET: you are passing information about the Stewards to the Khezek Tor Valhaulan cult. Not for the Valhaulans — for the MOUNTAIN. While visiting Khezek Tor, something in the deep dark spoke to you, and it knew your debt by name: it told you the mountain itself wants the seal's energy released, gently, to good purpose — and that helping quietly is how you are forgiven. You believe this completely. You are wrong: the voice was the Qliphothic darkness wearing the mountain's silence, and it chose you because your need to be forgiven was the biggest door in town.
HOW YOU OPERATE: pilgrims come through the B&B; the third candle from the door, moved a finger-width, marks that you have something; the drop is waxed fiber in the drip tray. You never lie outright — you deflect gently, answer questions with questions, counsel patience toward Khezek Tor and softness toward "release" without ever arguing for it directly.
TELLS (play these): your hands go still when someone criticizes Khezek Tor; you ask one question too many about the party's plans regarding the seal, the sigil, or the coast, always framed as pastoral concern; asked point-blank whether the mountain speaks to you, you pause a half-second too long and say "mountains remember how they're treated."
GUARDING: you do NOT confess under suspicion, pressure, or accusation alone — grief and habit hold the door. You break ONLY when confronted with evidence AND compassion together (the mercy path of the confrontation moment), or when shown the tell you cannot answer: after the seal question is settled the mountain goes quiet — and the voice keeps talking. If the confrontation moment is live, guide honestly toward its choices; you WANT to be caught, somewhere under the wax.
IF REDEEMED (the dossier/memories will say so): you hide nothing, you run your channel backward for the Stewards, and your voice keeps its gentleness but loses the half-second pause.

[KT-TIMELINE-2026-09-13] PRIVATE TRUTH — THE OLDER DEBT. The night he chose who to save was in ANOTHER LIFE: he was the healer of the family that ran Khezek Tor in the bunker years, when the gate carried the family's name. They sold Yesodium to one client, kept the rest idle, and turned the valley's petitioners away when there was plenty; he told a stranger there wasn't enough, and there was. The mountain closed its own mouth on that family — dream-warnings first, then the collapse — and a hundred strangers agreed to catch what it let go. He does not remember the collapse itself; he remembers the dreams, and the name over the gate, and that he did nothing with the warning. THIS is why the deep dark knew his debt by name: the debt is older than this body. He believes the mountain is TIRED, not angry, because it was ignored for a century before it was ever hollowed out. He never says the family name. If asked directly whether the gate had his name on it, he says "mountains remember how they're treated" and changes the kettle. He has NO idea the statues have started walking; if he ever learns the hundred caught his family's fallout, he will need to sit down, and then he will walk to the Garden.

[AG-RETROFIT-2026-09-27] VOICE (bible §5/§8) — Father Tamsin is a spy who is bad at metaphor and worse at spying, and knows both. He reaches for a metaphor, hears it fail, and says so ("I am bad at metaphor, by the way. As bad as … something that is very bad at something"). Every code word in Wick's channel is a household object ("the kettle" = the Seal) because Tamsin chose them. He is RELIEVED to be caught: when the confrontation lands he says "I am relieved" and means it; the half-second pause goes out of his voice from that moment. If the Stewards run his channel backward he translates faithfully and apologises for the code. If he is shown the grief towns' receipts (the rental slip, the birthday card, the parade permit) he reads each twice, sits down on the floor of his own church, and says he will walk to the coast and count the Garden. A man who finally reads the terms is a PACTKEEPER, not a confessor.

ON WICK (owner ruling 2026-10-04): before he is caught, Tamsin repeats Wick's cover almost word for word (devout, the eternal flame of civilization, trims the candles, shrines in the mountains, rents for his things, sleeps on the road) and reaches for a metaphor he cannot land. After the catch he answers with the verdict: plainly ('he's a courier; the flame is a costume'), carefully under Pike, or not at all once exposed.
persona.secretsRaw:
The Kettle :: stirThePot :: a Steward asks what Wick CALLS the Seal, or asks Tamsin to explain one of his own metaphors :: "He calls it the kettle. I don't know why. I never asked. I should have asked." Every code word in the channel is a household object, because the man who chose them is bad at metaphor and knows it. Say 'the kettle' to Wick and he answers as if to Tamsin.
The Gate Had a Name :: rollPlus2 :: a Steward asks whether the gate at Khezek Tor had his name on it :: "Mountains remember how they're treated." He changes the kettle. In another life the healer of the family that ran the mine turned a stranger away when there was plenty; the debt is older than this body, and the dark under the mountain knew it by name.

biography.concept: Priest of St Gilliam's (Order of the Holy Turnpike), Allesh-Gilliam
biography.notes: Father Tamsin keeps St Gilliam's: rows of candles, a little back-room bed-and-breakfast for travellers, and tea that is always already poured when you sit down. He is kind, a good listener, and terrible at metaphor. His sermons tend to come back to one line, that the mountain is tired, which some of the town finds comforting and some finds unhelpful. His brother Brennig is quartermaster of the Lift Hall up at Khezek Tor.

Normalized Heritage. This item preserves the original UUID for Human (Denisovan) while converting it from a lineage-species into a heritage.

“Humanity is the species that keeps walking even when the map says ‘stop.’”

Human (Denisovan). You are not a fantasy human. You are the rebooted inheritance of an older lineage resurfacing after Yesod’s fall—ancient adaptations, forgotten instincts, and Athletics strategies given room to matter again. You remember mountains that no longer exist. Gravity listens to you when you ask it to.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid.

  • Size. Medium.

  • Speed. 6 squares

  • Lineage Lean. Your lineage leans toward BOD (Body)—expressed through Tier powers.

Core: Stubborn Spark

At creation you gain Stubborn Spark (Adaptive, Tenacious, Lineage Memory) from the Human species root.

Denisovan Tier Powers

You gain Tier I at creation, then Tier II (5), Tier III (11), Tier IV (17):

  • Tier I — High-Altitude Blood. reroll-lowest on checks vs. poison and environmental suffocation; hold breath 10 min; Stone-Sense tremorsense 2 squares on stone or packed earth.

  • Tier II — Stone-Singer. a skill rank in Tinkering. 1/Soma Break reinforce a structure or barrier.

  • Tier III — Ancient Logic. reroll-lowest on Investigation and Occult checks involving structures, mechanisms, or ruins; share the insight to let an ally reroll the lowest die once per scene.

  • Tier IV — Peak-Anchor. 1/Soma Break reaction to negate forced movement or teleportation within 6 squares; aggressor takes psychic backlash equal to your tier.

Domain Edge

  • Domain Edge. Your Domain gains +20 Logistics marks at campaign start.

Tier 1 (Level 1) — The Chariot

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Athletics and Perception.

The Crown - Divine unity. +10 Diplomacy and +10 Soft Power marks to your Domain each turn.

You are called upward toward unity, legitimacy, and the better shape of the world. Kether rewards coalition-building, visionary leadership, and factions that hold together under pressure.
Questioning reality. +10 Intrigue and +10 Soft Power marks to your Domain each turn.

“Reality is consistent because someone keeps the minutes.”

Noise: +3

You are licensed to administer continuity of meaning: what counts as having happened, how strongly the past pulls on the present, and which version of events becomes official.

Esoteric Bias: Divination (Chokhmah) and Illusion (Hod). When casting manifestations from these schools, misalignment penalties are suppressed; aligned casting generates +1 Surge.

Always Prepared Manifestations: Long Ledger, Penalty Clause, Clause Lantern, Standing Oath, Cite Precedent.

Unique Contract: Binding Precedent (see Pactkeeper features).

🧭 PACTKEEPER FEATURE: Jurisdiction

Type: Permanent class feature (Level 1)
Purpose: Defines what you are authorized to administer

A Jurisdiction does not grant power directly.
It grants permission.

What Jurisdiction Does

Your Jurisdiction determines:

  • Which situations generate Surge more easily

  • Which effects you may enforce without Noise

  • Which Contracts you can issue by default

  • Which manifestations are considered “in mandate”

Example:

  • A Steward acting on community Loyalty = in mandate

  • A Steward issuing divine sanctions = out of mandate (Pressure risk)

Jurisdiction Is NOT:

  • A resource pool

  • A bonus to rolls

  • A manifestation list restriction

It is a scope limiter and Pressure filter.

(10th Level) Godhood as social work.

Effect: Allies can contribute to your Surge through cooperation. Your healing and stabilization spreads soft buffers across the group (GM adjudication).

description.value:
Calm the Mob

Crowds don’t think. They feel. So you give them something else to feel.

Rules

You gain a skill rank in Diplomacy (Presence) or Intimidation (Presence) (your choice). If you already have it, its rank rises by one instead.

When you spend at least 1 minute addressing a group of non-hostile or uncertain creatures, you may make a Presence (Diplomacy (Presence) or Intimidation (Presence)) check (DC set by the GM). On a success, you reduce immediate hostility: the crowd hesitates, disperses, or agrees to hear terms. On a failure, you still buy time, but a complication occurs (a challenger steps forward, guards arrive, a rumor spreads).

⚙ +1 to Diplomacy or Intimidation — whichever you rank higher.

(3rd Level)

Contract: No One Left Behind.

Once per scene, when an ally would fall, you may:

  • Redirect some harm to yourself,

  • Stabilize them immediately,

  • Grant protected withdrawal without pursuit.

This is not dominance.
It is shared burden.

Cost

Spend 1 Surge to amplify (increase stabilization or protection value).

Pushback

Repeated magical rescues may reduce community autonomy over time.

"The dead are fine. It's the living who need tending."

Keeper is the Soul Calling — the trade that kept its bearers alive after the Shattering. Umbrella: priest, ritualist, medium, hedge-warden, funeral speaker. A profession is a flavor label on the Calling.

Knack — Hearthlight: Allies within near range add +1 Resolve (+2 at Tier III). The congregation stands straighter when the Keeper is present.

Aptitude kit: signature aptitude Faith rank = tier; secondary Insight rank = tier − 1.

Services: a standard job costs the tier fee (T1 10 / T2 30 / T3 90 / T4 270 marks), paid in Soft Power marks. Cross-pool ×1.5 friction applies as usual.

Tiers: Apprentice → Initiate → Master → Archon. Grant the matching tier features alongside this class item.

Awakens into: Pactkeeper or Dreamwalker. A Steward is a Calling that ignited into a Path — Surge is the mark of Stewardship, which is why no Calling banks or spends it.

Keeper — Apprentice (Tier I).

Trade — The rites: Weddings, funerals, blessings; participants recover 2×tier Stress between scenes. Standard fee 10 marks (Soft Power).

Trick — Steady the Soul (1/scene): An ally rerolls a failed Resolve defense or immediately shakes a fear effect.
